'''Thaddeus Charles Young Sr.''' (born June 21, 1988) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]], before being selected 12th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. In 2018, Young became the 5th player in NBA history with at least 800 games to average 13.5 points, 5.9 Rebounds, 1.4 steals, 49% FGS, and 30% 3PT FGS, after [[Larry Bird]], [[Magic Johnson]], [[Michael Jordan]], and [[LeBron James]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fox Sports Indiana posts graphic comparing Thaddeus Young to LeBron, Jordan, Bird and Magic, gets roasted |url=https://awfulannouncing.com/nba/fox-sports-indiana-graphic-compares-thaddeus-young-to-lebron-jordan-bird-and-magic.html |date=2018-02-28 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Young was born to Lula Hall and Felton Young<ref name="prospectprofile">[http://www.nba.com/draft2007/profiles/ThaddeusYoung.html Thaddeus Young - Prospect Profile]</ref> in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]].<ref name="wreck">[http://www.ramblinwreck.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/young_thaddeus00.html Thaddeus Young Bio]</ref> His family moved to [[Memphis, Tennessee]] when Young was in [[fourth grade]]. His father played basketball for [[Jacksonville University]] from 1976 to 1978,<ref name="wreck" /> and was selected by the [[Buffalo Braves]]<ref name="prospectprofile" /> in the 8th round of the [[1978 NBA draft]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1978.html 1978 NBA Draft – Basketball-Reference.com]</ref>

===High school career===
Young began playing varsity basketball in the [[eighth grade]], and while attending [[Mitchell High School (Tennessee)|Mitchell High School]], he rose to the top of the high school player ranks. His athletic honors included being named to the all-state team three times, being named the [[TSSAA]] [[Tennessee Mr. Basketball|Class AA "Mr. Basketball"]] in 2005, being named the 2006 Tennessee Gatorade Player of the Year and being named to the [[McDonald's All-American Game]]. In 2006, he led Mitchell's basketball team to the TSSAA Class AA finals against [[Liberty Technology Magnet High School]]. As a [[twelfth grade|senior]], he averaged 26.9 [[point (basketball)|points]], 13.8 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 4.1 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], 4.3 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] and 3.6 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] per game. He was an excellent overall athlete at Mitchell who also excelled in [[cross country running|cross country]] in his [[eleventh grade|junior year]].<ref name="wreck" /> Young was an exceptional student at Mitchell who graduated with a 4.3 [[Grade Point Average|GPA]].<ref name="wreck" /><ref>[http://www.utsandiego.com/sports/college_basketball/20061107-9999-1s7fabfrosh1.html Fab Frosh]</ref> Coming out of high school Young was one of the most prized [[recruiting (athletic)|recruits]] of the 2006 freshman class.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080105175333/http://www.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/stories/110905abb.html Tech Signs Four Basketball Players to Letters-of-intent]</ref>

==College career==
Young was the youngest member of [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]]'s 2006 freshman class.<ref name="wreck" /> Young finished his freshman season with averages of 14.4 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 2.2 assists.<ref name="stats">[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/thaddeus-young-1.html Thaddeus Young Stats]</ref> He shot a solid 47.8% [[field goal percentage|from the field]] and an above average 41.9% from the [[three-point field goal|three-point line]].<ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==
===Philadelphia 76ers (2007–2014)===
[[File:Thad Young.jpg|thumb|left|Young with the 76ers in March 2013]]
On June 28, 2007, Young was drafted by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 12th overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nba_news/sixers_youngsmith_070711.html Sixers Sign First-Rounders Young, Smith]</ref>

In his [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] debut on November 7, 2007, Young made his first NBA [[field goal (basketball)|field goal]] at the [[Wachovia Center (Philadelphia)|Wachovia Center]] in [[Philadelphia]] in a 94–63 76ers' win over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. Young finished the night with 6 points and 3 rebounds.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200711070PHI.html Charlotte Bobcats at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, November 7, 2007]</ref>

Until [[General manager#Sports teams|general manager]] [[Ed Stefanski]] was hired, Young did not play very often. After the trade of [[Kyle Korver]], Young played more minutes and alternated with [[Reggie Evans]] in the starting lineup. Young averaged 8.2 points, 4.2 rebounds, and 21 minutes per game during 2007–08. His season high in points was 22 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on March 9, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080313001802/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=280309015 Sixers kick off long stretch with easy win over Bucks]</ref> He played a total of 74 games, starting 22.

On February 5, 2009, Young was selected to play in the 2009 Rookie Challenge as a member of the Sophomore team.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/2009/allstar2009/01/28/rookie_rosters.allstar09.012809/ Durant, Rose among players in 2009 Rookie Challenge] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222131915/http://www.nba.com/2009/allstar2009/01/28/rookie_rosters.allstar09.012809/ |date=February 22, 2014 }}</ref>

In game 3 of the 76ers' 2009 opening round playoff series against the Orlando Magic, Young made a game-winning shot with 2 seconds remaining to give Philadelphia a 2 games to 1 lead.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=anfjSPxMKTA Thaddeus Young's Game-Winner]</ref>

On March 7, 2010, Young recorded a career high 32 points in a 114–101 win over the Toronto Raptors.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20100312185422/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=300307028 76ers sharp behind arc to end five-game skid with win over Raptors]</ref>

On February 21, 2014, Young set a career high with 29 field goal attempts, going on to record 30 points, 13 rebounds, 6 assists and 7 steals in a 112–124 loss to the Dallas Mavericks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20140221/DALPHI/gameinfo.html Notebook: Mavericks 124, 76ers 112]</ref>

Young finished the [[2013–14 NBA season]] with career highs in points, steals, assists, three-pointers made, and games started. He also finished the season third in the league in steals.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/stats/player?season=2014&seasontype=2 NBA Player Steals Statistics - 2013-14]</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2014–2015)===
On August 23, 2014, a three-team trade was completed involving the 76ers, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], and the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. As part of the deal, Young was traded to the Wolves, along with [[Andrew Wiggins]] and [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]], both then of the Cavaliers. The Cavaliers received [[Kevin Love]] from Minnesota, whereas the 76ers received [[Luc Mbah a Moute]] and [[Alexey Shved]] from Minnesota and a 2015 first round draft pick from Cleveland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/love-three-team-trade|title=Timberwolves Acquire Andrew Wiggins, Anthony Bennett and Thaddeus Young in Three-Team Trade|date=August 23, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|access-date=August 23, 2014}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2015–2016)===
On February 19, 2015, Young was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Kevin Garnett]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nets/nets-acquire-thaddeus-young-minnesota Nets Acquire Thaddeus Young From Minnesota] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221194152/http://www.nba.com/nets/nets-acquire-thaddeus-young-minnesota |date=February 21, 2015 }}</ref> On June 22, 2015, Young opted out of his contract with the Nets to become a free agent.<ref>[https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2490011-thaddeus-young-opts-out-of-nets-contract-latest-details-comments-and-reaction Thaddeus Young Opts out of Nets Contract: Latest Details, Comments and Reaction]</ref> On July 9, 2015, he re-signed with the Nets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-brook-lopez-and-thaddeus-young |title=Player Signing Press Conference |work=NBA.com |date=July 9, 2015 |access-date=July 10, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711235023/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-re-sign-brook-lopez-and-thaddeus-young |archive-date=July 11, 2015 }}</ref> On February 3, 2016, he recorded 16 points and 14 rebounds against the Indiana Pacers, setting a new single-season career high with his 22nd double-double.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160203/INDBKN/gameinfo.html C.J. Miles scores 27, Pacers beat Nets 114-100]</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2016–2019)===
On July 7, 2016, Young was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Caris LeVert]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-acquire-teague-young-trades Pacers Acquire Teague, Young in Trades]</ref> On November 23, 2016, he scored a season-high 24 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngth01/gamelog/2017/ Thaddeus Young 2016-17 Game Log]</ref> On December 10, 2016, he scored 24 points and hit a career-high six 3-pointers in a 118–111 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899790 George has 37 points to lead Pacers over Blazers 118-111]</ref>

On November 1, 2017, Young scored a season-high 26 points against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngth01/gamelog/2018/ Thaddeus Young 2017-18 Game Log]</ref>

On December 17, 2018, Young was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for Week 9 of the 2018–19 season, marking his second career Eastern Conference Player of the Week award and his first honor since January 2014 when he was a member of the Philadelphia 76ers.<ref name="l771">{{cite web | title=Thaddeus Young Named Eastern Conference Player of the Week | website=NBA.com | date=2018-12-17 | url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/thaddeus-young-named-eastern-conference-player-week | access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref>

On January 17, 2019, Young scored a season-high 27 points in a 120–96 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pacers-thaddeus-young-drops-team-high-27-points/|title=Pacers' Thaddeus Young: Drops team-high 27 points|work=cbssports.com|date=January 18, 2019|access-date=January 22, 2019|quote=...which explains his season-best scoring effort.}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2019–2021)===
On July 6, 2019, Young signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]] as a free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-thaddeus-young|title=Bulls sign Thaddeus Young |date=July 6, 2019|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> Following his first season with the Bulls, Young improved during his second season, with 12.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 4.3 rebounds, and 55.9% shooting.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Bulls' Thaddeus Young wins 2020-21 NBA Hustle Award {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/bulls-thaddeus-young-wins-2020-21-nba-hustle-award |access-date=2026-04-24 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> Eventually, the power forward inserted himself as a starter for the Bulls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Expect Bulls to stay with Tomas Satoransky and Thad Young in starting lineup for now {{!}} Chicago Bulls |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/gameday/expect-bulls-stay-tomas-satoransky-and-thad-young-starting-lineup-now |access-date=2026-04-24 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> He was the winner of the [[NBA Hustle Award]] that season.<ref name=":0" />

===San Antonio Spurs (2021–2022)===
On August 11, 2021, Young, [[Al-Farouq Aminu]], and several draft picks were traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in exchange for [[DeMar DeRozan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/san-antonio-completes-trade-chicago|title=SAN ANTONIO COMPLETES TRADE WITH CHICAGO|work=NBA.com|date=August 11, 2021}}</ref>

===Toronto Raptors (2022–2024)===
On February 10, 2022, Young, [[Drew Eubanks]], and a 2022 second round selection were traded to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[Goran Dragić]] and a 2022 first-round draft selection.<ref>{{cite web|author=sasemauricio|title=SPURS ACQUIRE GORAN DRAGIĆ & 2022 FIRST ROUND PICK|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-acquire-goran-dragic-2022-first-round-pick|website=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 10, 2022}}</ref> On June 30, Young signed a two-year, $16 million contract extension with the Raptors.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raptors' Thaddeus Young: Staying in Toronto|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/raptors-thaddeus-young-staying-in-toronto/|website=CBSSports.com|date=June 30, 2022|access-date=July 1, 2022}}</ref>

On February 8, 2024, Young was traded alongside [[Dennis Schröder]] to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Spencer Dinwiddie]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Schröder and Young from Toronto Raptors|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-schroder-and-young-from-toronto-raptors|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}}</ref> but was waived that day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Complete Three-Team Trade with Phoenix and Memphis|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-complete-three-team-trade-with-phoenix-and-memphis|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024|quote=In a related move, Brooklyn has requested waivers on forward Thaddeus Young.}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2024)===
On February 20, 2024, Young signed with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN FORWARD THADDEUS YOUNG|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-forward-thaddeus-young|website=NBA.com|date=February 20, 2024|access-date=February 20, 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Young and his wife, Shekinah Beckett, have two sons named Thaddeus Jr. and Taylor.<ref>[http://www.playerwives.com/nba/philadelphia-76ers/thad-youngs-fiancee-shekinah-beckett-a-playerwivescom-exclusive-interview/ Thad Young's fiancee Shekinah Beckett: A PlayerWives.com exclusive interview]</ref>

In May 2011, Young started a foundation called ''Young for Youth'' to help at-risk youth and young families.<ref>[http://youngforyouth.org/about/ Welcome to the Young for Youth Foundation!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812201700/http://youngforyouth.org/about/ |date=August 12, 2014 }}</ref>

Young's mother, Lula Hall, died on November 13, 2014, after an 18-month battle with breast cancer; she was 57 years old.<ref>[https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/wolves-wear-pink-shoelaces-in-honor-of-thad-young-s-late-mom-024624121.html Wolves wear pink shoelaces in honor of Thad Young's late mom]</ref>
